findings.evidence: Proof obtains `c : Fin (N+2) → ℝ` with `∑ c i • (moment vectors) = 0` and `∃ i, c i ≠ 0` from `Fintype.not_linearIndependent_iff` — a statement about the whole kernel, not one witness; the conclusion at lines 143-145 keeps only `∃ p`. Roadmap README:448-451 requests the family form.
findings.fix: State the family: e.g. `⊥ < (Polynomial.degreeLT ℝ (N + 2)).comap/inf of {p | ∀ n ≤ N, ∫ x in Icc a b, x ^ n * p.eval x = 0}` (or that this submodule contains a nonzero element and lies in `Polynomial.degreeLT ℝ (N + 2)`), and derive the present existential from it. `Polynomial.degreeLT` and `Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Basic.lean:55,114) give the ambient `(N+2)`-dimensional space; the linear-dependence argument already in the proof supplies the kernel element.
findings.issue: `exists_polynomial_ne_zero_setIntegral_Icc_pow_mul_eq_zero` yields a single polynomial, but the dimension-count proof (lines 147-155) establishes a nonzero kernel of the `N+1` moment functionals on the `(N+2)`-dimensional space of polynomials of degree `< N+2`. The docstring at lines 139-140 asserts the stronger subspace statement ("The counterexamples therefore form a nonzero subspace of an explicit `(N + 2)`-dimensional space") that the theorem does not state, and the roadmap target asks for "the explicit finite-dimensional family of counterexamples" (roadmap README line 451).

findings.evidence: grep for `setIntegral_Icc_sub_midpoint_eq_zero` in `code/` returns only its declaration (line 192) and the two docstring mentions (lines 29, 43) — no use site. `Set.Icc a b = ∅` when `b < a`, so `∫ x in Icc a b, _ = 0` needs no order hypothesis.
findings.fix: Either drop the lemma, or restate it as the explicit `N = 0` instance under `hab : a < b`: `p := Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C ((a + b) / 2)` with both `∫ x in Icc a b, x ^ 0 * p.eval x = 0` and `¬ (fun x => p.eval x) =ᵐ[volume.restrict (Icc a b)] 0`, so it genuinely specialises `exists_polynomial_ne_zero_setIntegral_Icc_pow_mul_eq_zero` instead of restating a weaker computation.
findings.issue: `setIntegral_Icc_sub_midpoint_eq_zero` is a separately proved special case with no consumer anywhere in the repo, and it is weaker than the `N = 0` instance the PR proves in general: it omits the `¬ =ᵐ[volume.restrict (Icc a b)] 0` clause that the file itself (lines 131-134) says is what makes a counterexample sharp, while the docstring and module header (line 29, 43) present it as "the lowest counterexample". Its hypothesis `hab : a ≤ b` is also stronger than the statement needs: for `b < a`, `Icc a b = ∅` and the integral is `0`, so the equation holds unconditionally.

summary: The determinacy half sits at the right level, but the sharpness half states strictly less than its proof and its own docstring deliver (one existential witness instead of the counterexample subspace the roadmap asks for), and the midpoint lemma is an unused, weaker special case of the general theorem with a removable hypothesis.
